docs(pretty): describe the Pretty renderable that exists, not the repr protocol that doesn't (rich-docs-site-13t.3)

The ticket named the `richReprAuto` decorator. Grepping `richRepr` across `src/`
returns nothing — and neither do `rich.angular` or any other repr hook, so the
whole "Custom object representation" section was fiction, not just its last
subsection. It is deleted. Per the epic's direction, no repr protocol was
implemented to make the page true; the code is the truth and the page moves.

Deleting it left a page whose remaining claims were also false, and the premise
was the worst of them. The page opened with "`print()` and `log()` automatically
format containers." They do not. `Console.print` renders any non-renderable
through `String()` (src/core/console.ts, the `else` branch of the item loop), so
a plain object becomes the literal text `[object Object]` — which `renderMarkup`
then parses as a style tag and consumes. Printing an object prints a blank line.
`Pretty` is never reached unless you construct it. Every section is rewritten
around that.

Four sections then documented options that do not exist where they were shown.
`console.print(data, { indentGuides: false })` does not configure anything:
`PrintOptions` recognises only `style|justify|markup|highlight|overflow|end|
softWrap|crop|sep`, so the options object falls through as a second *value* to
print and disappears the same way. The options belong to `Pretty`'s constructor,
and the page now says so with the failing form shown beside the working one.

Both output blocks were fabricated, in four ways each: `│` indent-guide glyphs
(the guide is a `dim green` *space* — `Style.parse("repr.indent")`, applied by
`_addIndentGuides` to one space per level), two-space indents (the default is 4),
Python `'single'`-quoted keys and strings (keys print unquoted, strings via
`JSON.stringify`), and Python `True`. The `maxString` block claimed
`'…' +240 chars`; the real suffix is `+240` inside the quotes, as part of the
string. Every output block on the page is now captured stdout at width 43, and
the width is stated in the lead because it decides compact-vs-expanded.

New, and true: a class instance formats as a plain object from its own enumerable
properties, with no class name — which is the honest replacement for the section
that promised a repr hook. `Map` and `Set` have no one-line form. The compact-fit
test measures a container without the key it sits under, so a nested container
can overrun by the length of its key (filed separately).

Verified by extracting all nine ```typescript blocks verbatim, writing each to
its own file, rewriting the `@promptctl/rich-js` specifier to `src/index.js`, and
running `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` plus vitest over all nine. Per-file
isolation is what proves each block carries its own imports and `Console`. Gates:
`npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean, `npm run test` 2113 passing.

* docs(group): make every snippet on the page one that actually runs (rich-docs-site-13t.2)

The ticket named one defect — `RenderGroup`, which does not exist; the real
export is `Group` (src/renderables/group.ts). Renaming it was not enough. Every
example on the page failed at runtime, and the fix is the same fact in three
places: `Group`'s constructor is `(...renderables: Renderable[])`, strict, with
none of the string coercion `Panel` does via its own `toRenderable`.

- The "correct" constructor example passed bare markup strings to `Group`.
  `Group.render` calls `renderable.render(options)` straight through, so a
  string threw `TypeError: yield* (intermediate value) is not iterable`. Markup
  now goes through `renderMarkup`, which parses it into a `RichText`.
- The generator example passed the generator as a single positional argument,
  which throws the same way for the same reason. It is now spread —
  `new Group(...buildContent(...))` — matching the idiom already pinned by
  test/renderables/group.test.ts ("accepts spread from a generator").
- The output blocks showed each item on its own line. A group inserts nothing
  between its children, and `RichText.render` emits a line break only when its
  text ends in `\n` (the default `end` is appended by `console.print`, not by
  rendering — src/core/text.ts, the `_end !== "\n"` guard). Every item now
  carries its `\n`, which is what makes the printed blocks true, and the rule
  is stated in prose so the next reader does not rediscover it as a bug.
- "Generator / decorator form" was a fourth ghost. `@group` is a Python Rich
  decorator with no counterpart here; the heading is now
  "Building a group from a generator".

Every block was executed against src/ and the output blocks are its captured
stdout at width 43, not hand-drawn. Gates: `npm run docs:build` clean (dead-link
and Vue-interpolation gate), `npm run lint` clean. `RenderGroup` no longer
appears in the built site.

* docs(group): make each section stand alone, and stop calling a silent drop an error

Review caught that the generator block declared none of the four names it
used. It inherited them from the block above, so a reader copying that one
section got the global `console` — which has no `.print` — and three undefined
bindings. My verification had missed it because I ran all three blocks in one
test file, where the imports were already in scope; the check confirmed the
code was right and could not see that the block was incomplete. Each block now
carries its own imports and `new Console()`, matching the two above it.

Re-running the blocks one file each also falsified the `✗` comment. It claimed
Panel's two-argument form is an error, and the page said `// error` before this
branch. It is not: every field of `PanelOptions` is optional, so a `RichText`
is structurally assignable to it and the call compiles, runs, and drops the
second argument without a word. That silence is the thing worth warning about,
so the comment now says it and the output block shows both panels — the
one-line result of the wrong form above the two-line result of the right one.

Verified by extracting every ```typescript block from the page verbatim,
writing each to its own file, and running `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit`
plus vitest over all three. Gates: `npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean.

* docs(group): show the blank line print leaves, and name the error the compiler actually gives

Two claims on the page were still not what the code does.

The two-panel output block showed them flush against each other. They are not:
`Panel` ends with its own `Segment.line()` and `Console.print` then appends
`end` unconditionally (console.ts:449, where the comment explains it must go
through `_writeSegments` or `exportText` would join consecutive prints onto one
line). Two separate prints therefore always leave a blank line between them.
Captured the raw bytes by swapping `process.stdout.write` — the joined output
is `╯\n\n╭` — and the picture now shows that. Merging the two calls into one
print would have made the illustration match, but the section exists to show a
wrong call beside a right one, and printing them separately is the point.

The closing warning said the unspread generator "throws at render time." It
does not; it never reaches runtime. `Generator<RichText, void, unknown>` has no
`render`, so the argument is not assignable to `Renderable` and tsc rejects the
call. I had tested that sentence in a test file where `as never` forced the
argument past the compiler — the cast is what made the claim true there and
false on the page. The page now quotes TS2345 verbatim, which is what the
reader sees in their editor.

Verified as before: every ```typescript block extracted from the page verbatim,
each written to its own file, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` plus vitest
across all three, and both output blocks diffed against real stdout at width 43.
Gates: `npm run lint` and `npm run docs:build` clean.
